description: We are Team Organized Processors!  Combining NASA GISS & POWER open data with our AI assistant (ASTRA), we built COSMO for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. We decode past climate anomalies and simulate future carbon policies with our interactive What-If engine. Investigating Earth's trends together to shape a sustainable future!
summary: COSMO is an interactive web platform that translates NASA's global Earth observation datasets (GISS GISTEMP v4 and NASA POWER API) into accessible, localized insights for regions like Bursa and Şanlıurfa. By combining 3D Earth visualization, Python-based data processing, and a Gemini-powered AI assistant (AURA), COSMO simplifies complex environmental metrics. It features a COP31-aligned "Climate Policy Simulator," empowering users to test What-If carbon emission reduction scenarios interactively. This project addresses the challenge of data accessibility by bridging the gap between raw scientific data and everyday understanding, enabling students, researchers, and citizens to explore environmental trends, grasp regional climate impacts, and make data-driven decisions.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

COSMO is a web-based platform that transforms NASA's complex and raw global Earth observation data into understandable, localized, and interactive insights.

  • Working Principle: The platform utilizes reliable data sources such as NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 (historical temperature anomalies) and the NASA POWER API (regional meteorological metrics).
  • These datasets are processed and analyzed in the background, allowing users to query them through interactive 3D Earth visualizations, Python-based data pipelines, and a Gemini-powered AI assistant (ASTRA / AURA).
  • For instance, it operationalizes global data by tailoring it to local climate trends in specific regions like Bursa and Şanlıurfa.

2. What Are the Benefits and Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Eliminating the "Climate Blindspot": By bridging the gap between global climate data and local reality, it enables ordinary citizens and regional stakeholders to see how climate changes specifically affect their own areas.
  • Accessibility and Awareness: Allows non-scientists—including students, educators, researchers, and the general public—to easily examine complex climate data.
  • COP31 Climate Policy Simulator: Thanks to the interactive "What-If" carbon emission reduction slider integrated into the project, users can test future climate scenarios firsthand and experience the impacts of policy decisions.
  • Intended Impact: Eliminating passive data consumption to foster an active, participatory, and data-driven conscious society while enhancing climate literacy.

3. Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Used

  • Data Sources (APIs & Datasets): NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 and NASA POWER API.
  • Programming Languages & Libraries: Python and Pandas (for cleaning, aggregating, and scaling time-series data).
  • AI Integration: Google Gemini API-powered ASTRA / AURA AI assistant (to explain analytical findings in natural language and generate smart responses to user queries).
  • Visualization & Interface: Interactive 3D Earth visualization tools and web interface technologies.

4. Project Creativity and Critical Factors Considered by the Team

  • Creativity: It stands out by going beyond static and boring climate charts, combining a 3D Earth, natural language AI querying, and an interactive policy simulator into a single unified platform.
  • Critical Factors Considered by the Team:
    • Scientific Transparency: A clear boundary has been established between AI-generated text and mathematical/statistical calculations based on raw data, prioritizing the traceability of data sources.
    • User-Centric Design: An intuitive experience catering to the needs of diverse target audiences (students, researchers, the public) has been targeted.
    • Connecting Global Goals with Local Context: An end-to-end solution has been structured that blends the global climate crisis and COP31 goals with the realities of local regions (cities).
